analysis: MARKET & PORTFOLIO REVIEW: SPY is in a confirmed uptrend (+4.86% 20d slope) but the portfolio's recent history is sobering — 5 consecutive stop-outs (FICO, IQV, ADP, MSFT, ZBRA) with a profit factor of 0.69x. This signals either bad luck in a choppy period or a tendency to enter too early before trends confirm. Discipline demands we not chase to recover losses. EXISTING POSITIONS: A (+4.47%) — thesis intact; Agilent is quality healthcare instruments, no thesis break, hold with existing stop. LII (+11.32%) — performing well; HVAC/cooling beneficiary with durable pricing power. No reason to exit. Both positions are small relative to equity; no over-concentration. NEW TRADES: With 69% cash, the market in uptrend, and 2 basing setups offering genuinely asymmetric risk/reward, I am proposing 2 new positions to bring the book to 4 concentrated names. CI (Cigna) is the cheapest quality large-cap on the screened list at fwd P/E 8.43 with $6.9B FCF, basing right at SMA50 with slope turning positive — classic Stage 1-2 transition. CDW is a quality technology distributor in a confirmed uptrend basing pattern, with fwd P/E 10.90 and strong FCF, sitting only 36% into its 52w range with meaningful upside to prior highs. Both have ~35-40 days before earnings which provides adequate runway. ADP is excluded despite reappearing on the list — too soon after a stop-out psychologically and the pattern of -3.56% stop suggests the trend needs more time to repair. WDC, ADI, CSCO, NXPI are all extended (80-90%+ of 52w range, 10-33% above SMA50) — late-cycle entries forbidden by hard rules. Remaining candidates are either too close to earnings (<25d), have declining EPS revisions, or lack the asymmetry needed. After these two trades: A+LII+CI+CDW = 4 positions, ~79% deployed, ~21% cash reserve.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $281 or better; ideally on a pullback to or slight bounce off the SMA50 (currently ~$283). Do not chase above $285.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Cigna trades at fwd P/E 8.43 and PEG 0.84 — among the cheapest quality names in the S&P 500. FCF of $6.9B provides substantial capital return capacity. Healthcare insurance is a defensive, recurring-revenue model with pricing power. EPS revisions are flat (not deteriorating). TECHNICAL: Price is in the 48th percentile of its 52w range — midfield, not extended. MIXED/SIDEWAYS basing with the SMA50 slope now positive (+2.5% over 20d) signals transition toward Stage 2. Price is hugging the SMA50 (only -0.5% below), and SMA200 is flat to positive — this is a controlled basing setup, not a falling knife. ATR of 2.3% allows a 2x ATR stop at ~4.6% without hitting the ceiling. Earnings are 34 days out, providing a full month of runway before binary risk.
trades.exit_plan: Primary exit: target $315 (near 52w high/prior resistance) or stop at $268.91. Thesis-break exits: if SMA50 slope rolls negative again, or if the stock closes more than 2 consecutive sessions below SMA200 on volume. Earnings management: reduce or exit ahead of July 30 earnings if position is flat/negative; hold through earnings only if sitting on >7% unrealized gain. Time stop: reassess at 10 weeks if no material progress toward target.

trades.entry_strategy: Buy near current price ($128); set limit at $127.50. Prefer entry on a mild intraday pullback rather than chasing. SMA50 at ~$124 provides backstop.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: CDW is a high-quality technology solutions distributor with ROE of 44.2%, operating cash flow of $1.2B, and FCF of $884M. The fwd P/E of 10.90 is strikingly cheap for a business of this quality — the market appears to be discounting cyclical IT spend concerns, which creates the asymmetry. Revenue growth of +9.2% and positive EPS revisions (+3.6%) confirm the business is not deteriorating. High D/E (240x) is structural for a distributor using working capital leverage — not the same risk as a capital-intensive industrial with that ratio. TECHNICAL: Confirmed UPTREND with basing pattern. Price is only 36% into its 52w range, well below the 52w high of $179.37 — significant upside runway. SMA50 slope is positive (+3.1%), price is +2.9% above SMA50 (modest, not extended), and the base has formed above SMA50 — classic Stage 2 entry. ATR of 4.3% with a 1.5x stop produces a 6.4% stop — within the acceptable 4-15% range. Earnings Aug 5 (40d) gives adequate runway.
trades.exit_plan: Primary exit: target $160 (prior consolidation resistance, ~25% gain). Stop: $119.77. Thesis-break: exit if price falls back below SMA50 and SMA50 slope turns negative — that would indicate the uptrend is failing. Earnings management: tighten stop to breakeven if entering the final week before Aug 5 earnings with less than 10% gain. Time stop: if stock makes no progress in 8 weeks, exit and redeploy elsewhere.
